method: One bounded 24-source-label early-history local amateur/prep/church/fraternity/civic/AAU identity tranche; source-named organizations preserved without unsupported legal genealogy or roster continuity. Identity adjudication only; accepted Stage 1 game universe not reopened.

source_identity_families.identity_basis: SDSU original 1921-22 opponent explicitly identifies Army-Navy Academy (JC). Contemporary 1921 academy advertisement lists curriculum from seventh grade through Junior College at Pacific Beach; early 1921 school identity predates the 1936 move to Carlsbad. Preserve its historic academy college-level opponent apart from later secondary-school cadet programs.

Original source identifies a Buchan Bakers team, not an educational institution. Independent SDSU-specific opponent series corroborates a single 1954-55 match. Canonical identity is the named team only; exact bakery company, geography and organization charter are not proved by this source.

The primary team name is explicitly Central Christian Church in 1924-25. Preserve its source-defined church team independently from University Christian Church; no proof establishes that either congregation, team or venue is the other.

Source identifies an Escondido Creamery-affiliated opponent for 1927-28, not Escondido High School or a varsity college. Company legal entity and basketball roster remain unverified; use the source-named business team without invented corporate history.

Source names a specifically designated All-Star squad associated with National City in 1927-28. Keep distinct from the 1921-22 'National City' source-named team and the 1925-26 National City Baptists; no shared membership inferred.

Independent opponent series validates the 1925-26 National City Baptists label and a single match. Baptists church basketball team distinct from other National City and National City All-Stars opponents, despite same city qualifier.

Source says Bank League All-Stars rather than a specific bank-sponsored club. Preserve distinct from accepted First National Bank SDSU team and unadjudicated Bank of Italy team; composition and league charter unknown.

SDSU source enumerates four 1926-27 through 1930-31 DeMolay games; independent SDSU series reproduces four, including one source-designated postseason game. DeMolay is a separate source-named youth fraternal-team identity, without presuming a particular chapter or that 'DeMolay' equals any other YMCA/church squad.

San Diego History Center historical research records the SDSU-associated Hod Club becoming Eta Omega Delta fraternity, and a City of San Diego 1997 resolution documents its separate fraternity existence through the 1947 Kappa Sigma initiation. This is the campus FRATERNITY opponent basketball team named in 1923-26 source records, never the SDSU varsity team or a fabricated duplicate SDSU game.

Independent SDSU series enumerates exactly two Fletcher Five games matching original 1925-26 and 1931-32 literals. No assumption that same five individuals played in both seasons; original '(D)' retained as raw source notation.

Independent historical SDSU series explicitly calls the 1926-27 opponent Grossmont HS Alumni, distinct from the separately mapped Grossmont High School varsity program. Preserve accepted source postseason category; not evidence of ordinary NCAA postseason format.

The 1921-22 SDSU literal says only National City, without organization suffix. Do not claim this was the later Baptist or All-Star squad, a high school, or any particular club. Provisional source-specific identity with membership uncertainty declared.

Original 1924-25 source explicitly identifies a Ramona High School opponent. This is a high-school team, not a college or generic 'Ramona' municipality; precise campus/history beyond the source is not claimed; original '(D)' preserved.

A source-named team of San Diego basketball coaches in 1928-29, corroborated by independent 1928-12-13 SDSU opponent series. This is not a current-D1 institution or a team called San Diego State; refrain from roster and site inferences.

Independent SDSU series confirms original 1921-22 30-13 game against explicitly county-wide All-Star named team. Distinct from San Diego YMCA All-Stars and other city specific teams; no roster or geographic site assumptions.

Contemporary March 1946 Oklahoma City Times identifies San Diego Dons as an AAU team, runner-up in 1946 national AAU tournament; independent San Diego State series confirms three 1944-47 SDSU meetings. This is a San Diego AAU team and NOT University of San Francisco Dons or University of San Diego Toreros; exact year-to-year sponsorship/roster not asserted.

Original SDSU 1927-28 label and independent SDSU series explicitly identify an ALUMNI squad distinct from the previously resolved Sweetwater High School varsity opponent. Keep original source game type, including any postseason note, unchanged.
Independent SDSU opponent series corroborates exactly two 1925-26 Todd's All-Stars games. Source team preserved without inventing which Todd, sponsoring entity, court or roster.

Original 1922-23 label and independent SDSU series corroborate precisely one University Christian Church opponent. Distinct from source-named Central Christian Church in 1924-25; 'University' in a church name does NOT imply a college program.

Original source names USC Dentists, not the University of Southern California varsity Trojans. Keep separate amateur dental-student/faculty subunit opponent identity. No unsupported inference regarding the exact roster, school affiliation beyond USC suffix or an on-campus physical site.

Independent SDSU opponent series validates one 1937-38 contest against a Whittier Junior Chamber of Commerce basketball team. Not Whittier College's varsity Poets or Whittier High School; no exact civic club charter presumed.

Original SDSU source uniquely names Hancock's All-Comets in 1922-23. Retain this exact historical team label instead of merging with other 'All-Stars', and do not assume Hancock's business, player's identity or home location.

Original 1934-35 source names Hanson’s All-Stars team, distinct from the named Hancock's All-Comets, Todd's All-Stars and later San Diego County All-Stars. No unproven captain, roster, employer or venue assertions.

key_separations: National City (1921 source team) distinct from National City Baptists and National City All-Stars
University Christian Church distinct from Central Christian Church
Grossmont High School Alumni distinct from Grossmont High School varsity
Sweetwater High School Alumni distinct from Sweetwater High School varsity
San Diego Dons AAU distinct from University of San Francisco Dons or USD Toreros
Army-Navy Academy historical junior-college unit distinct from modern secondary-prep team
Eta Omega Delta Hods fraternity opponent distinct from San Diego State varsity
USC Dentists subunit distinct from USC varsity
Fletcher Five two source notations retain separate dates, no invariant roster inference
exclusion_reason: Remaining labels have distinct touring-team or historical game-inclusion/forfeit concerns; source-named local amateur identity tranche does not authorize Stage 1 reopening or blanket exhibition classification.
